name: content-edit
title: Content edit: the typed write, and the baseline restore proved by defining twice

steps.note: Evidence 213 (FSAMP3 + FEDIT1). '.content define' writes DestroyData.DestroyReason Default(0) -> Consume(2) through TryRead<T>/Write<T> and reads it back; '.content drop' disposes the editor, which restores Core's captured baseline; the SECOND '.content define' must print 'Default(0) -> Consume(2)' AGAIN. Had the baseline not been restored, the before value would read Consume(2). That second read is the whole case.
Start from a known state: if the second item is not registered this replies that nothing was dropped.

steps.expectLog: Sample content: edit read-back: handle\.Guid=-?\d+ TryRead<PrefabGUID>=-?\d+ \(equal, so the editor was handed the clone and not the source prefab\)
Sample content: edit write: ProjectM\.DestroyData\.DestroyReason Default\(0\) -> Consume\(2\) via TryRead<T> then Write<T>
Sample content: edit write read-back: Read<DestroyData>\(\)\.DestroyReason=Consume\(2\) \(equal to what Write<T> was given, so the write stuck\)

steps.note: The restore proof: the same before value a second time.

steps.expectLog: Sample content: edit write: ProjectM\.DestroyData\.DestroyReason Default\(0\) -> Consume\(2\) via TryRead<T> then Write<T>

steps.note: Leave the world as the case found it.
